A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PQMass and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Inspection of all 14 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2 supports comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original null tests, sampling-method evaluations, mode-dropping and time-series experiments, MNIST training measurements, CIFAR-10 assessments, and a Bayesian experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on image corruption, missing classes, tabular data, astrophysical images, protein sequences, distance metrics, and permutation calibration.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 1 selects reference points from one sample set and includes them in the counts. v2 Section 2.2 selects references from both sets and removes them before counting. v2 also changes the main p-value calculation to the upper tail, removes the Bayesian variant, and introduces optional permutation calibration in Appendix I.

E1.justification: v2 adds FFHQ256, ImageNet, Adult Census, Probes, SKIRT TNG, JWST detector images, and ESM Metagenomic Atlas sequences. Coverage also expands to class-omission, small-mode, corruption, scaling, and rotation scenarios. The original Gaussian-mixture mode-dropping and time-series experiments remain in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Appendix H adds weighted and unweighted Schilling nearest-neighbor tests as direct statistical comparators. Figure 8 adds C_T and authenticity-score comparisons to the memorization experiment, although those metrics already appeared in v1's human-judgment comparison. Wasserstein, MMD, and JSD comparisons remain; FLS and FLD refer to the same cited Jiralerspong et al. method.

E3.justification: The Gaussian-mixture null evaluation expands from a stated sample size of 5,000 to a 128–16,384 sample-size sweep. New experiments introduce controlled class removal, noise corruption, geometric perturbations, and a 50-samples-per-distribution comparison. The reported VAE learning-rate decay changes from 0.1 to a factor of 0.9 every 50 steps; whether existing training curves were regenerated is unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds MNIST class-dropping, small CIFAR-10 mode detection, ImageNet corruption, distance-metric sensitivity, permutation calibration, and qualitative failure analyses. These test sensitivity and validity beyond v1's analyses. The CIFAR-10 hyperparameter ablation is retained, while the Bayesian translated-distribution validation is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix I introduces permutation-based p-values for the mean over dependent retessellations, substantially extending statistical calibration. v2 also reports 2^14 null-test repetitions, replacing v1's inconsistent statements of 200 in the text and 500 in the caption. Existing reporting of standard deviations over 20 tessellations remains in several comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the CIFAR-10 ablation table retain their numerical results. Substantial new results include FFHQ evaluations, missing-mode tests, astrophysical comparisons, and permutation tests. For example, v2 Table 2 reports ImageNet PQMass values increasing from 95.55 to 4495.07 across noise variances 0 to 1. The Bayesian likelihood curve is removed.

T1.justification: v2 introduces quantized-measure definitions and two consistency propositions with proofs under explicit smoothness and support assumptions in Section 2.3. It removes the Bayesian likelihood and posterior-predictive derivations. The main p-value integral changes substantively from the lower tail in v1 Equation 12 to the upper tail in v2 Equation 5.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains sample-based generative-model assessment without fitting auxiliary models. v2 narrows headline scalability to moderately high-dimensional data and frames the abstract's test around multinomial bin-count equality. Its introduction adds upper-bound language and qualifies general applicability by requiring a definable metric.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds substantive limitations concerning small samples, extreme region counts, unsuitable tessellations, correlated model outputs, and distance metrics. Appendices G and I explain scaling blind spots of cosine/correlation distances, dependence between retessellations, and permutation-testing tradeoffs. These materially qualify the earlier broad applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future implementation release; v2 supplies a repository link. v2 newly documents MCMC subsampling, tabular encoding, sequence distances, simulation settings, astrophysical sample allocations, and A100 runtime information. Hyperparameter documentation is revised, although v1's explicit VAE batch size of 512 is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around scientific inverse problems, simulation-based inference, privacy, and synthetic-content detection. It adds Voronoi-theory references, Schilling's two-sample tests, and literature supporting the new application domains. Several Bayesian-integration and alternative-sampling references disappear; publication updates to retained works are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and theoretical exposition are extensively rewritten. Separate theory and algorithm sections become Theory and Methods; image experiments are consolidated, and time-series and Gaussian-mixture analyses move to Appendix F. A dedicated limitations section and reorganized appendices substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensively resized and repositioned displays. Figure 2 becomes a sample-size comparison; the human-judgment figure gains an FFHQ row, and the memorization figure expands from two to four panels. Numerous new plots and tables accompany the added analyses, while the Bayesian figure disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validity gaps by separating reference selection from counted samples, correcting the main p-value tail, and providing permutation calibration for dependent retessellations. New stress tests and explicit limitations make sensitivity and applicability substantially easier to assess, while the repository link improves reproducibility information. The Bayesian branch is lost, and both versions still overinterpret p-values as probabilities of hypotheses, but the calibration and validation gains support a substantial overall improvement.
